decision: Retain the measured CPU-package RAPL curve and the explicitly derived additive +120 W curve as separate graph HTTP benchmark evidence.
accepted_findings: The exact 16-ID SQLite graph HTTP workload completed all 13 tested concurrency levels with zero failed responses.
Concurrency 1 was fastest at 954.2 servings/s. Across concurrency 8 through 128, throughput ranged from 435.4 to 460.9 servings/s and median CPU-package power ranged from 104.1 to 110.9 W.
At concurrency 8, the fastest concurrent point was 460.9 servings/s at 108.58 W measured RAPL package power; the derived offset-adjusted median is 228.58 W.
The new run had 2.5–6.1% lower throughput and 16.3–26.0 W higher package power than the previous clean sweep at concurrency 1, 4 and 8; cause is unresolved.
claims_not_supported: The adjusted wattage is a direct measurement of whole-system power.
CPU utilization reached 100%, a thermal limit, or a hardware maximum.
The run-to-run package-power change has a known cause.
The graph benchmark establishes production serving capacity or a PLM advantage.
